digest.component_or_area: store push core and reconcile-bridge workflows
propositions: A 106-line CAS push loop in reconcile-bridge.yml (lines 272–377) duplicates logic in push.py (lines 161–296) with divergent retry budgets (5 vs 3) and missing final-push after clean merge.

Strict-mode push delivery must raise a catchable exception carrying git reason and unpushed-commit count on every silent best-effort return path (malformed config, missing remote, policy decline, transport failure, rebase guard, store-epoch guard, merge-clean terminal, lock timeout, and off/async contradiction), with non-zero exit and stderr only at the private module CLI boundary.

Both reconcile-bridge.yml and reconcile-bridge-canary.yml YAML loops must be deleted and replaced with core entrypoints (commit-and-push --strict and push --strict) that accept explicit author identity and unconditionally delegate to a shared five-cycle-plus-final-push push core.

All existing best-effort callers (event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, both delete paths, both compact paths, claim) must inherit the durability correction (five merge cycles and final push) while remaining best-effort and preserving return/disposition contracts unchanged.

The reconciler passes commit message 'chore: sync events from rebar reconciler [run ${{ github.run_id }}]' unchanged and receives author name/email from BRIDGE_BOT_NAME/BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL environment variables.

Strict mode must fail loud and non-zero when sync.push resolves to off or async (configuration contradiction with synchronous-delivery guarantee), while best-effort mode preserves current off/async behavior unchanged.
